newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares catch breath ahead of H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares catch breath ahead of H1 results.

text.p: Estonian shares were mixed on Tuesday as the market caught its breath after last week's surge and waited for first half results and a possible revision of profit forecasts, dealers said
Total trade on the main list was 41.3 million kroons with the Talse 0.06 percent lower at 276.07.
"Prices should stay stable for the rest of the week, but the focus is on the banks' half-year results," a dealer said.
Several banks are expected to revise their profit forecasts in the coming week following better than expected results for the year so far.
Hansapank closed at 147.15 kroons, up 0.15 kroons after turning over 16 million kroons.
"There was nothing driving Hansapank, it was down slightly in Helsinki and there are no rumours of exceptional results for June," a trader said.
Hoiupank was also up one kroon to close at 151.25 kroons after registering trade of 11.7 million kroons.
Its price was pushed up by expectations that Sweden's Swedbank would increase a stake in it.
Just before the bourse closed, Swedbank confirmed that it had signed an agreement to purchase 7.4 percent of Hoiupank's shares from the central bank, raising its stake to 19.9 percent.
The free market remained very quiet with no stock's trade topping one million kroons.
Diversified industrialist Norma was the most active with 670,850 kroons traded to hold at 73 kroons.
